text:
Detroit led 4-1 in Sunrise with a period to play and lost. That is the night, and for a Red Wings team that has now dropped five straight, it is a hard one to sit with.

The early part went Detroit's way, and not always because of great chances. Sam Reinhart opened the scoring at 3:52 and J.T. Compher answered 15 seconds later. Andreas Englund then scored unassisted on a 2% look, Lucas Raymond made it 3-1 17 seconds into the second, and Marco Kasper tipped in a Moritz Seider shot for 4-1. Seider, who had two assists in 26:30, has been speaking about leading the room without a captain, and that is the story hanging over this team: Dylan Larkin, the captain, is refusing to play until he is traded, and the headlines this week are about which team, Minnesota or Montreal, will meet Detroit's price.

Florida's comeback started with 18 seconds left in the second, when Gustav Forsling scored off a Carter Verhaeghe pass. Anton Lundell made it 4-3 early in the third. The Panthers then drove the period, out-chancing Detroit 2.66 to 0.79 in expected goals. Lars Eller batted one in at 16:29 to tie it, a goal that took Florida's win chance from 11% to 52%, and 51 seconds later Lundell finished a Brady and Matthew Tkachuk play for the winner. Verhaeghe had three assists.

Detroit had one more chance to steal a point. With the score 4-4, Akira Schmid denied Andrew Copp on a 48% look, the biggest save of the night by our numbers. Schmid otherwise had a tough game, allowing 1.1 goals more than expected, and John Gibson at the other end gave up five on 29 shots.

The process favored Florida all along: 63 shot attempts to 46, 4.36 expected goals to 2.9, and a 74% deserved-to-win share. Detroit's lead was built on low-percentage finishes, and the Panthers kept coming until the math caught up. The two teams have now split their season series after Detroit won 5-3 on Nov. 2.
headline: Panthers erase three-goal hole, Red Wings' slide hits five
